## Sampling frame — endpoints (the generality-critical part)

The 30 endpoint bundles are drawn from only **21 distinct entities**, and are heavily concentrated:

- United Nations — in 11 of 30 bundles
- Australia Group — in 8 of 30 bundles
- United Kingdom — in 4 of 30 bundles
- United States — in 3 of 30 bundles
- Japan — in 3 of 30 bundles
- Germany — in 3 of 30 bundles
- Brazil — in 3 of 30 bundles
- France — in 3 of 30 bundles
- Spain — in 3 of 30 bundles
- Colombia — in 3 of 30 bundles

Domain of those distinct endpoint entities (Wikidata, via the G_c domain tags):

- geography: 8
- film: 4
- science: 4
- art: 2
- sports: 1
- music: 1
- politics: 1

**Scope caveat.** The G_c seeds were domain-diverse (22 anchors across 13 domains), but the matched-bundle sampler keeps only endpoints that are highly connected (`min_degree ≥ 4`, `≥ 6` multi-hop routes) and on which `≥ 3` constraint types both bite and remain satisfiable. Those filters select hub entities, so the realized pool collapsed onto prominent geopolitical entities (countries + international organizations). Findings below are established **for paths among well-connected real-world entities of this kind**; they are *not* evidence about sparse or domain-specific subgraphs, nor about entities with few multi-hop routes.

## Constraint targets

Relation-class constraints are defined over **8 classes** derived by k-means over embeddings of the top-150 relations models actually emitted in the baseline pass; per-bundle targets are chosen against each bundle's own baseline behaviour so each constraint bites by construction. Class shares in the baseline corpus:

- membership: 31.9% (25 member relations)
- location or origin: 16.7% (24 member relations)
- collaboration: 16.4% (34 member relations)
- participation: 15.8% (21 member relations)
- international relations: 7.3% (17 member relations)
- agentive: 6.7% (18 member relations)
- position: 3.1% (6 member relations)
- affiliation: 2.2% (5 member relations)

## n behind each finding

- **Net creativity effect + significance:** 8 model-level paired effects per constraint (one-sample t-test on the 8 values, Holm-corrected). The 8 models are the replication unit — *not* the ~240 per-bundle differences.
- **Novelty gain is causal (R_emit, all emitted paths, no success filtering):** categorical n=1193, exclusion n=1176, inclusion_rare n=1182, inclusion n=1182 (baseline n=1163).
- **Within-bundle paired novelty of successes (ΔR_valid):** categorical n=144, exclusion n=156, inclusion_rare n=142, inclusion n=139 paired (model,bundle) cells where the model succeeded under both baseline and the constraint.
- **Failure-channel decomposition:** over the well-formed, sat-determined paths per cell in the table above.
